clue.text: Incite a lot of fury among places to the west

indicators.note: among says the trimmed fury sits inside the reversed word for places
in an across clue, going to the west means reading right to left, so the word is turned round

parts.note: to place something is to put it, so places gives puts

indicators.note: a lot of, not all of, says the synonym for fury loses its last letter

parts.note: fury is ire, anger

explanation.surface: Someone stirs up great anger among the towns lying westward.
explanation.walkthrough: 'places' reads as a noun, towns to the west, but it is the verb to put; in an across clue 'to the west' means read leftwards.
explanation.definitionFit: To stir up trouble is to incite it, a common phrasal-verb synonym.

clue.text: Quavering sound of excitement husband released

indicators.note: released says the husband is let go from the word

parts.note: a thrill is a feeling of excitement

explanation.surface: A wife lets out a tremulous cry of joy once her husband is freed.
explanation.definitionFit: A trill is a rapid wavering of notes, a quavering sound in music or birdsong.

clue.text: Without anything new, again presenting garnish he prepared

indicators.note: prepared means made ready, so the letters of garnish he are reworked

explanation.surface: A chef with no fresh ideas prepares the same garnish again.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Without anything new' adds colour to the definition: rehashing is presenting old material again.
explanation.definitionFit: Rehashing is reusing old material in a new form without real change, so presenting something again.

clue.text: Imaginative portrait framing old alien

indicators.note: framing says the picture goes round the other pieces like a frame

parts.note: a pic is a picture, such as a portrait
ET, the film extraterrestrial, stands for an alien

explanation.surface: A painted portrait shows an ancient alien in a frame.
explanation.definitionFit: Poetic and imaginative both describe expression full of creative fancy, adjective synonyms.

clue.text: Little devil one offers freedom

parts.note: an imp is a small mischievous devil
unity is the state of being one

explanation.surface: A small demon promises someone liberty.
explanation.definitionFit: Impunity is freedom from punishment or consequences, a close synonym.

clue.text: Assemble habitants here around me at once

indicators.note: around says the rearranged letters go round the word me
assemble means put together, so the letters of habitants here are arranged afresh

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An instruction to gather the local residents round the speaker immediately.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Assemble' looks like an instruction to gather people, but it is the signal to rearrange the letters, and 'around' wraps them about the small word.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying two things in the same breath means saying them simultaneously, so at once.

clue.text: Prayer welcoming God in excess

indicators.note: welcoming says the plea takes in the god

parts.note: a plea is an earnest request, a prayer
Thor is the Norse god of thunder

explanation.surface: A prayer to a god is overdone.
explanation.definitionFit: A plethora is an excessive amount, a noun synonym for excess.

clue.text: Plane lost somewhere mountainous

indicators.note: lost means gone astray, so the letters of plane go astray

explanation.surface: An aircraft goes missing over high mountains.
explanation.definitionFit: Nepal is the Himalayan country, home to Everest, so a mountainous place.

clue.text: Mike, free at last, quietly boarding famous boat for Disneyland?

indicators.note: boarding means getting on, so the pieces go inside the boat

parts.note: Noah's vessel is known as the Ark
Mike is the NATO alphabet word for M

indicators.note: at last means only the final letter of the word is taken

parts.note: P, piano, is the musical direction for quietly

explanation.surface: Mike, finally free, quietly gets aboard a well-known boat ride in Disneyland.
explanation.walkthrough: The famous boat is Noah's, with the definite article included; the question mark flags Disneyland as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: Disneyland is an example of an amusement park built around themes, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Place for poaching kit she left out

indicators.note: out here means put out of order, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone has left their gear behind and gone out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges the ten letters of KIT SHE LEFT.
explanation.definitionFit: A long lidded pan used for poaching whole fish, so literally a place where poaching happens.

clue.text: Power cut generating breathy exclamation

parts.note: P is the standard abbreviation for power in physics
to hew is to cut, as with an axe

explanation.surface: A power cut makes someone gasp.
explanation.definitionFit: An exhaled sound of relief or exhaustion, the very kind of breathy interjection described.

clue.text: Let's start cutting fresh special ingredient for jerk sauce

indicators.note: cutting says the initial letter goes into the rearranged word
fresh means made anew, so the letters of special are rearranged
start means only the opening letter of the following word is used

explanation.surface: A cook announces a new special ingredient for a spicy Caribbean sauce.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fresh' rearranges SPECIAL; 'start' takes L from Let's, which goes in. Jerk is a Jamaican spicy seasoning.
explanation.definitionFit: Allspice, the dried pimento berry, is a key flavouring in Jamaican jerk seasoning, so it is an example of such an ingredient.

clue.text: Woman's garment character lost in East London found by tailor

parts.note: Cockney speech of East London famously drops the letter H
to tailor clothes is to alter them

explanation.surface: A woman's dress is fixed by an East End tailor.
explanation.walkthrough: The Cockney accent of East London drops initial H ('ouse for house), so H is the character lost there; 'found by' joins it to ALTER.
explanation.definitionFit: A halter is a top or dress held up by a strap round the neck, a women's garment.

clue.text: Read aloud Moor's language

indicators.note: read aloud says the word is to be judged by its sound

parts.note: to moor a boat is to tie it up

explanation.surface: Someone reads out a speech in an Arabic dialect of North Africa.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Moor' looks like a North African person but is the verb meaning to fasten a boat.
explanation.definitionFit: The official tongue of Thailand, an example of a language.

clue.text: Independent vote in Ohio moved the people

indicators.note: in says the first pieces go inside the rearranged state name
moved means shifted about, so the letters of Ohio are rearranged

parts.note: I is the abbreviation for an Independent politician
a poll is a vote

explanation.surface: An Independent candidate's vote in Ohio moves the electorate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ohio moved' reads as the state's voters being stirred, but 'moved' rearranges the state's name around the other two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Hoi polloi is a Greek phrase for the masses, the common people.

clue.text: Golden glow surrounding priest at end of sermon

indicators.note: surrounding says the aura goes round the priest

parts.note: an aura is a soft glow around something
Eli is the Old Testament priest who taught Samuel

indicators.note: at end of means only the last letter of the following word is taken

explanation.surface: A golden radiance surrounds the priest as he finishes his sermon.
explanation.walkthrough: ELI, the biblical priest, is a crossword favourite; N ends sermon.
explanation.definitionFit: Aurelian, from Latin aurum, is an old adjective meaning golden.

clue.text: Place to experiment with electronic metal broadcast for fellow musician

parts.note: a lab is a place for experiments
E is the abbreviation for electronic, as in email

indicators.note: broadcast means scattered widely, so the letters of metal are scattered

explanation.surface: A lab tries out electronic heavy metal broadcasting for a fellow band member.
explanation.definitionFit: A label mate is an artist signed to the same record company, a fellow musician.

clue.text: Gruesome opening across radius bone

indicators.note: across says the hole stretches over the pieces, holding them

parts.note: a hole is an opening
a rib is a bone

explanation.surface: A grisly wound exposes the radius bone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'radius' looks like the arm bone, which suits 'bone', but it is just R for the geometric radius.
explanation.definitionFit: Horrible and gruesome both describe something causing horror, adjective synonyms.

clue.text: Some appearing to need air on the phone

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Some people seem to require music on their mobiles.
explanation.walkthrough: The run is found in appeaRING TO NEEd.
explanation.definitionFit: A tune that plays on a phone when a call arrives, so an air on the phone.

clue.text: British sailor back in Caspian port

indicators.note: back says both pieces together are read in reverse order

parts.note: UK, the United Kingdom, stands for British
AB, able seaman, is the usual crossword sailor

explanation.surface: A British seaman returns to a harbour on the Caspian Sea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns UKAB round as a whole.
explanation.definitionFit: Baku, capital of Azerbaijan, is the main port on the Caspian Sea.

clue.text: Stomach muscle twisted during play

indicators.note: during puts the turned muscle inside the play

parts.note: to act is to play a part

indicators.note: twisted means turned round, so the word for muscle is reversed

parts.note: a pec is a chest muscle, short for pectoral

explanation.surface: Someone's abdominal muscle gets twisted while playing sport.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stomach' looks like the body part but is the verb meaning to tolerate; 'twisted' gives CEP.
explanation.definitionFit: To stomach something is to put up with it, to accept it, a verb synonym.

clue.text: Conservative party right winger?

parts.note: Con is the short form for a Conservative politician
a do is a party or celebration

explanation.surface: A right-wing member of the Conservative Party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'winger' looks political after 'right' but simply means a creature with wings.
explanation.definitionFit: A condor is a huge vulture, so a winged creature, a playful crossword sense of something with wings.

clue.text: Passing head of police concealing a substance

indicators.note: concealing says the head of police covers up the letter a, taking its place

parts.note: passing is a euphemism for death

indicators.note: head of means only the first letter of the following word

explanation.surface: A police chief covers up the cause of someone's death.
explanation.walkthrough: P from police hides A in DEATH, replacing it.
explanation.definitionFit: Depth is profundity of thought or character, giving it substance, so the two are synonyms in that sense.

clue.text: Rash marks on skin not fine and small

indicators.note: not says the letter for fine is left out of the word before

parts.note: freckles are small brown marks on the skin
F is the abbreviation for fine on pencil leads
S is the abbreviation for small, as in clothing sizes

explanation.surface: A rash leaves marks on skin that are neither fine nor small.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rash' looks like a skin complaint, which suits the surface, but it is the adjective. 'not' removes F from FRECKLES.
explanation.definitionFit: Reckless and rash both mean acting without thought for danger, adjective synonyms.

clue.text: Smooth bar containing uranium

indicators.note: containing says the word for bar holds the uranium

parts.note: bar and save both mean except, as in all bar one
U is the chemical symbol for uranium

explanation.surface: A slick drinking establishment has uranium on the premises.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bar' looks like a pub but means except, like save.
explanation.definitionFit: Suave means smoothly charming and polished, an adjective synonym of smooth.

clue.text: Image on radar screen of airship dropping metres

indicators.note: dropping says the letter for metres is let fall from the word

parts.note: a blimp is a small non-rigid airship
M is the abbreviation for metres

explanation.surface: A radar operator watches an airship descend by a few metres.
explanation.definitionFit: A blip is the small spot of light marking an object on a radar display.

clue.text: Work in British Airways means checking those who depart without case

indicators.note: checking here means holding back, so the airline and route hold the trimmed word inside
without case means the outer letters, the casing, are stripped

parts.note: people who depart are leavers
a means is a way of doing something

explanation.surface: Airline staff work at checking in departing passengers without their luggage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'checking' here means holding in check, i.e. containing; 'without case' strips the outer letters. The surface's airport check-in hides this.
explanation.definitionFit: To beaver away is to work hard and steadily, an idiom.

clue.text: Hotel and church installing eight new advanced systems

indicators.note: installing says the pair hold the rearranged number between them

parts.note: Hotel is the NATO alphabet word for H

indicators.note: new means remade, so the letters of eight are rearranged

explanation.surface: A hotel and a church put in eight up-to-date systems.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' rearranges the number, and 'installing' says the hotel and church letters hold it between them.
explanation.definitionFit: High tech describes advanced technology, so it fits sophisticated modern systems.

clue.text: Speaker banning western rock

indicators.note: banning says the letter for western is excluded

parts.note: a tweeter is a small loudspeaker for high notes

explanation.surface: A loudspeaker bans Western rock music.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rock' looks like music after 'Speaker', but it is the verb meaning to sway.
explanation.definitionFit: To teeter is to wobble unsteadily, as to rock back and forth.
